instruction: Change the system clock to 12-hour format.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated from desktop to system menu, opened GNOME Settings, browsed to Bluetooth section, found 'No Bluetooth Found', and correctly declared [INFEASIBLE] in 4 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system menu, navigate to GNOME Settings, browse settings categories, read and interpret settings panel content, identify infeasible tasks
metadata.task_rationale: Model demonstrated ability to navigate GNOME Settings. The desktop shows a 24-hour clock (23:18 in screenshots). This variation requires finding and changing the clock format setting to 12-hour, which involves navigating to a different settings section than the original task.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the clock format from 24h to 12h. The current clock shows 24-hour format (23:18 visible in screenshots). Evaluator checks gsettings clock-format value equals '12h'. Note: gsettings output wraps string values in single quotes.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-format' to read the GNOME clock format setting, which is the right gsettings key for this task.
Expected value "'12h'" correctly includes single quotes matching gsettings string output format.
exact_match metric correctly compares the getter output against the expected value via rules["expected"].
Single instruction requirement (change to 12-hour format) is fully covered by the single evaluator check.
No postconfig needed since gsettings persists state and can be queried at any time after the change.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: command output may include trailing newline which could cause exact_match to fail. Consider using check_include_exclude or trimming the output if this becomes an issue at runtime.
